transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My family and our accountant insisted I come in for a medical evaluation, which is why I'm here today. But I'm absolutely certain I'm seeing things more clearly than everyone else and that my ideas can't be wrong, even when my family says they make no sense.

Have you noticed any periods in your life where you felt unusually energetic, slept very little, or felt like your thoughts were racing, or do you feel like your current mindset has been stable for a long time?

Yes, for most of the past year since starting the farm expansion, I've been incredibly revved up and running on just three hours of sleep a night because my mind is constantly racing with ideas I can't shut off. This high-energy, wired state has pretty much been my main way of being lately, rather than my old stable self.

During these times when your mind is racing and you have all these big ideas, have you ever felt like you were hearing voices or seeing things that others couldn't, or felt like people were conspiring against you?

Yes, during those exact times I was racing around, I clearly heard a man's voice out in the fields and in bed warning me that my family was trying to sabotage my plans. I also became convinced—and still am—that the seed companies and co-op board are tracking my drones to steal my regenerative farming system. It all happened right at the same time I was feeling so wired and energetic.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports a persistent period of high energy, racing thoughts, and decreased sleep (consistent with a manic episode) accompanied by auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions. Because these psychotic features occurred specifically during the period of mood disturbance, the diagnosis of F31.2 (Bipolar disorder, current episode manic with psychotic symptoms) is now the primary candidate, while F31.1 is excluded as it does not account for the psychotic symptoms.

The presence of psychotic symptoms during a manic episode confirms Bipolar I Disorder, current episode manic, with psychotic features.
